subject: Help with a simple, normal hierarchical model

messages.author: 0171daa6c1685f47
messages.subject: Help with a simple, normal hierarchical model
parts:
Hello all,

I recently started using STAN. Here is a model I am trying to fit;
It runs, but shows the warning message that there were divergent transitions after warmup.
Also, any pointers to make my code efficient (or reparametrizing my model) will also be helpful.

Thanks
Natesh

data {
  int                T; // number of time instances
  int                N_pm; 
  matrix[T,N_pm]     y; 
  matrix[T,N_pm]     m; // estimated mean
  matrix[T,N_pm]     sigma; //estimate s.d.
  cov_matrix[N_pm]   R; // This will be the centering matrix for the Wishart
}

parameters {
  vector[N_pm]    b; //  random intercepts
  vector<lower=0>[N_pm]    tau; // variance for the random intercepts
   cov_matrix[N_pm]   W; //Covariance matrix
   matrix[T,N_pm]    mu;
}

model {
  b ~ normal(0,tau);
  for (i in 1:T)
   for(j in 1:N_pm)
        mu[i,j] ~ normal(m[i,j]+b[j],sigma[i,j]); 
  for (i in 1:T)
    y[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i],W); 
  // priors
  W ~ inv_wishart(N_pm, R);
  b ~ cauchy(0,3);
  tau ~ inv_gamma(1, 1);
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Help with a simple, normal hierarchical model
parts:
It's much more robust to parameterize in terms of Cholesky
factors. We prefer the LKJ priors on correlation matrices
scaled by a vector of scales---there's a description of how to
do this in the manual chapter on regression. And a paper
by Ben Goodrich showing why the LKJ priors make a lot more
sense than Wisharts (degrees of freedom parameter controls
prior concentration around unit matrix).

Also, you want to vectorize all those sampling statements for
efficiency.

To eliminate the divergences, you want to switch to a non-centered
parameterization (more efficient in both HMC and Gibbs). There's
a description in the manual.

- Bob
